observations: ScienceWorld online evaluation is described as a deterministic 660-task pool across seven sampled task types from the Hugging Face test split, using seed 42, shuffle-tasks and a frozen episodes list via --episodes-path episodes.jsonl.

For every task the paper says it records success, final environment score, episode length, retrieved entry IDs and token count, writer/dreamer events and bank size, streamed to per_task.jsonl, trajectories.jsonl and dreamer_calls.jsonl; aggregate summary.json reports success rate, mean score, bank sizes, wall-clock and role LLM/token counts.

The paper describes LanceDB per run_id with Qwen2.5-3B embeddings and dynamic refresh, and uses Qwen3.5-9B as ScienceWorld task agent with Qwen3-14B writer/consolidator components on the inspected configuration surface.
Appendix dataset statistics for the original ScienceWorld release are 3,604 train and 1,802 test examples.
The public trace corpus README reports 3,592 ScienceWorld train episodes and 1,819 ScienceWorld test episodes and exposes rollout trajectories plus memory-writer outputs.

The public generic Dataset Preview currently fails schema generation with a column-casting mismatch across heterogeneous JSONL files; this is a viewer/schema-loader limitation and is not evidence that raw JSONL bytes are corrupt.
The inspected model page is public but has no model card or visible paper-run binding semantics on the card surface.

Tree/history inspection was blocked by a Hugging Face cache miss during this invocation; direct fallback also encountered transient network/DNS failure, so absence of a manifest inside the repository is not claimed.
The inspected page identifies a Qwen3-tagged Safetensors checkpoint of about 15B parameters in BF16 and no inference provider.
The card surface has no model card or visible evaluated-run/split/consolidation-output binding semantics; file-tree inspection was transiently cache-blocked.

findings.title: Auto-Dreamer paper localizes the missing historical replay package to concrete run-export files
findings.observation: The paper explicitly names a frozen episodes.jsonl and per-task/run exports per_task.jsonl, trajectories.jsonl, dreamer_calls.jsonl and summary.json. These are sufficient needles for future public-artifact discovery and materially narrow the causal replay gap from an unspecified missing trace to a specific unlocated export package.
findings.scope_guard: The paper's description proves intended logging semantics, not that the historical files are publicly released or immutable-bound to a reported run.

findings.title: The reported ScienceWorld online evaluation population is a frozen 660-task subset, not the full public test trace corpus
findings.observation: The paper describes 660 ScienceWorld evaluation tasks across seven sampled task types with seed 42 and a frozen episodes.jsonl, whereas the public trace corpus README reports 1,819 ScienceWorld test episodes. Therefore public test-corpus availability alone cannot certify identity with the reported evaluation population.
findings.scope_guard: No claim is made that the 1,819-row trace corpus is incorrect; a derivation or episode-manifest bridge can legitimately map it to the 660-task evaluation set.

findings.title: Original benchmark split counts and public collected trace-corpus counts are non-equivalent artifact populations
findings.observation: The paper reports original ScienceWorld split statistics of 3,604 train / 1,802 test, while the public Auto-Dreamer trace-corpus README reports 3,592 train / 1,819 test episodes. Count non-equivalence blocks any implicit one-to-one identity claim without an explicit derivation manifest.
findings.scope_guard: This is not a contradiction finding: the paper statistics describe the original benchmark split while the Hugging Face repository describes collected rollout trajectories plus writer outputs, so different counts may be expected.

findings.title: Public checkpoint pages still lack visible evaluated-run binding and tree inspection is transiently blocked
findings.observation: auto-dreamer-ckpt-bridge-public and dreamer_sciworld_v2_step60 are public and the ScienceWorld checkpoint exposes high-level model metadata, but the inspected card surfaces do not bind checkpoint bytes to a paper run, frozen episode manifest or consolidation output. Repository tree/history retrieval was cache/network blocked this invocation.
findings.scope_guard: Transient retrieval failure is an unresolved continuation item, not evidence that such files do not exist.

findings.title: Generic Hugging Face Dataset Preview is not a reliable replay schema for the heterogeneous Auto-Dreamer corpus
findings.observation: The dataset viewer currently raises a schema/casting generation error across heterogeneous JSONL files. Static audit should therefore bind raw file identities and file-specific schemas rather than relying on the viewer-generated unified table.
findings.scope_guard: Viewer failure does not imply raw artifact corruption or invalidate file-level audit.

checked_surface_negative.result: The checked public search/model-card/dataset-card surfaces did not expose a paper-run-bound ScienceWorld export bundle with these files.
checked_surface_negative.scope_guard: Checked-surface negative only; repository histories, mirrors and unindexed artifacts remain open.

full_causal_replay.reason: The exact 660-task episode manifest, public run-export files, checkpoint/run binding, serialized pre/post memory rewrite transactions and verifier/environment binding are not yet co-packaged on the inspected public surface. Live regeneration would require external model/compute execution and therefore is not an accepted zero-quota route.
